In the pharmaceutical industry, the term **"Big 3"** usually refers to the three massive companies that control wholesale drug distribution in the United States, though it can also describe the top global drug manufacturers. [](https://investingnews.com/daily/life-science-investing/pharmaceutical-investing/top-10-pharmaceutical-companies/)

These three corporations handle over 90% to 95% of all prescription drug logistics and delivery from manufacturers to pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics in the U.S. [](https://investingnews.com/daily/life-science-investing/pharmaceutical-investing/top-10-pharmaceutical-companies/)

- **McKesson Corporation**: The oldest, largest, and primary giant based in San Francisco, California.

- **Cencora** (formerly AmerisourceBergen): A major global healthcare solutions and drug sourcing leader.

- **Cardinal Health**

: A major global distributor headquartered in Ohio.

[](https://investingnews.com/daily/life-science-investing/pharmaceutical-investing/top-10-pharmaceutical-companies/)

### The Top Global Pharma Manufacturers

If you mean the largest drug-making and biopharmaceutical research corporations by revenue and market presence, the top tier globally consistently features:

- **Johnson & Johnson**: Regularly ranks #1 globally with massive pharmaceutical and medical device revenues.

- **Eli Lilly**: Surged to the top ranks alongside major market valuation driven by powerhouse metabolic and diabetes treatments.

- **Roche / Pfizer / Merck & Co.**: Compete closely for the remaining top manufacturing spots globally based on annual blockbusters and vaccine sales. [](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_biomedical_companies_by_revenue)
